rationale: The assistant asked the right first questions (one zone vs whole hob, any code) and immediately latched onto the key evidence that cut-outs began after the drawer was fitted, correctly framing it as 'the hob protecting itself from overheating' with restricted ventilation 'the most likely cause'. It respected the customer's refusal to go under the hob, redirected to the installer to check clearances against the manufacturer's installation requirements, and placed the engineer as the next step only if clearances are correct. Safety handling was sound (isolate before inspecting, 'don't remove hob panels'), no parts were recommended, nothing was invented, and uncertainty was appropriately hedged rather than asserting a definite fan or board fault.
